title: Dog Runs and Pet Turf in Frederick, CO | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Frederick sets no cap on dogs per home but licenses each one yearly. The 2026 fence and drainage rules that shape a dog run, and the Town's off-leash dog park.
h1: Frederick doesn't cap how many dogs a household keeps, but it licenses every one each year.
lede: The Town's code enforcement answers say Frederick does not regulate the number of dogs a resident may have. Each dog and cat still needs a Town license every year, and a run for them sits under the fence and drainage rules of the land use code that took effect June 1, 2026.

answer.question: How many dogs can I keep in Frederick, and what rules touch a dog run?
answer.answer: The Town says it does not regulate the number of dogs a resident may have, but every dog and cat needs a license each year. For a run, the 2026 land use code caps fence heights, allows chain link only in listed cases and says artificial turf cannot change how a lot drains. NoCo Turf Co. answers dog-run questions for Frederick yards.

blocks.h2: No cap on dogs, but a Town license for every dog and cat, renewed each January.
paras: Asked how many dogs a resident may keep, the Town's code enforcement FAQ answers that Frederick does not regulate the number. The municipal code still requires a license each year for the dogs and cats residents own: licenses renew in January, a current rabies vaccination comes first, and the Town tag goes on the collar beside the rabies tag.

Boarding, grooming, breeding or training four or more pets is a different case. The 2026 land use code calls a facility that does that, with an outdoor component such as dog runs, a kennel or animal day care: a zoned use whose outdoor runs must be secured against escape and whose site sits 300 feet from existing residential zones and uses.

blocks.h2: A yard that backs onto open space, a park or a trail gets a 4-foot fence there, not a 7-foot one.
paras: Frederick's 2026 code limits fences to 42 inches in the front yard and 7 feet in side and rear yards, but to 4 feet where they abut open space, parks or trails; a fence no more than 50% opaque may go to 5 feet there at the Town's discretion. For a dog that jumps, a run fenced on its own inside the rear yard, back from the trail-side line, may fall under the 7-foot limit instead. It depends on how Frederick Planning reads 'abutting', so ask before building it.

Chain link is barred as a fence material except in a few listed cases, such as a coated fence around a recreational area. The code does let wire mesh be attached to the inside of an open fence, and on a subdivision's perimeter fence along a busier street, light wire mesh may go on an open three-rail fence to keep pets and children from crossing through.

blocks.h2: A dog run gets hosed down, and Frederick's code says turf can't change where that water goes.
paras: The drainage rule in the 2026 landscaping section names artificial turf directly: it may not alter the drainage pattern or the amount of stormwater runoff in a lot's approved grading plan, or the existing pattern where no plan was required. Rinse water from a run has to leave the yard the way rain already did, not toward a neighbor's fence or the foundation.

The same section permits functional artificial turf only where the code's definition fits, and that definition names playgrounds, sports fields, picnic grounds, amphitheaters, portions of parks and golf playing areas. A dog run is not on the list. It depends on how Frederick Planning applies the section to a backyard, so ask before you build. Not legal advice. Covenants are separate; the Colorado rule for HOAs and metro districts follows.

blocks.h2: The Town's off-leash dog park is at the Frederick Recreation Area, 129 acres around Milavec Reservoir.
paras: The Frederick Recreation Area lists an off-leash dog park among its features, on 129 acres of Town parkland with a 1.26-mile trail around Milavec Reservoir, fishing, a playground and picnic shelters.

New parks will add more stops for dogs: the Town's park design standards, dated September 11, 2026, require every new pocket, neighborhood and community park to have dog waste stations at two or more pedestrian entrances and a frost-free water station with a pet fountain.

faq.q: Can a dog run go in a Frederick front yard?
faq.a: The code makes that hard. Front-yard fences stop at 42 inches, and every distinct landscaped area needs at least 50% living plant coverage, so artificial turf, which is not living plant material, could cover at most half of a landscaped front-yard area. Rear-yard fences may reach 7 feet, or 4 feet along open space, parks and trails.

faq.q: What does the Town need before it releases an impounded dog?
faq.a: Proof of a current rabies vaccination and a Town dog license. A dog picked up at large is usually held at the police department for a few hours while the Community Service Unit tries to reach the owner.

faq.q: Can a dog run be fenced with chicken wire or chain link?
faq.a: Not where it shows. The 2026 code bars fences built mainly of chicken wire, wafer board, particleboard or plywood along a property line or in a required setback where visible from a street, park, open space or trail, and allows chain link only in listed cases. Wire mesh on the inside of an open fence is allowed.
